# Overview

What is the climr App? Or perhaps the ClimApp?

## Structure

The climr App is organized into three tabs.

1.	__Get Data:__ Users can select points or areas of interest using one of 2 methods
    i.	Single map points or drawn polygons
    ii.	Uploading a shape file
    
      Users can then select the desired parameters and downscale the data. The downscaled data can be previewed and        is available for download as csv and GeoTIFF.
  
2.	__Visualization:__ Users can visualize data by choosing an area using one of 3 methods
    i.   Forest Landscape Plan (FLP) Area
    ii.  Ecoregions of North America
    iii. Single map point
    
      Users can then visualize data for the selected area using available plots (Bivariate, Walter-Lieth, Time      Series, Boxplot, Climate Stripes).
      
      Users can also add climate maps as an overlay on North America.

3.	__Documentation__: Help files and data sources
    a.	__Overview__: 
    b.	__Instructions__: Instructions on how to use the tool
    c.	__Methods__: Detailed background information about what's happening "under the hood"
    d.	__Known issues__: Documentation on current known issues with the tool
    e.  __Using the climr App for decisions__: Support and guidance for using the climr App as a decision-making tool
    f.  __Definitions__: Glossary of climate variables?
    g.  __Providing feedback__: Ways users can report issues or provide suggestions for future improvements
    h.  __FAQs__: Frequently asked questions
    i.  __Model information__: Version of input data and models
    j.  __Shiny app information__: Github repo, license, and other info
